question: to the Commission Maria Guzenina (S&D), Biljana Borzan (S&D), Maria Grapini (S&D), Mario Furore (The Left), Manuela Ripa (PPE), Magdalena Adamowicz (PPE), Stéphanie Yon-Courtin (Renew), Dimitris Tsiodras (PPE), Caterina Chinnici (PPE), Heléne Fritzon (S&D), Evin Incir (S&D), Adnan Dibrani (S&D), Sofie Eriksson (S&D), Johan Danielsson (S&D) Subject:

On 13 July 2026, the Commission’s Special Panel on protecting and empowering minors in the digital world presented its report to President von der Leyen. Its recommendations address key areas including age-appropriate design, digital literacy, platform accountability, support for parents and educators, children’s participation and the governance of digital services. Despite progress under the Digital Services Act, AI Act and Better Internet for Kids Strategy, children navigate an evolving ecosystem of platforms, social media, messaging, gaming, immersive environments and AI-powered services. This raises the question whether the EU framework is sufficiently coherent and future-proof to address the full range of risks and opportunities affecting children online. In the light of the above: 1.

Which recommendations in the Special Panel’s final report does the Commission intend to translate into concrete legislative and non-legislative initiatives, and what is the envisaged timeline for their implementation?

Is the Commission considering proposing a dedicated legislative instrument establishing a comprehensive framework for the protection, empowerment and participation of children in the digital ecosystem?

Does the Commission intend to develop a more holistic and future-proof approach to children’s digital rights, ensuring that legislation addresses the full digital ecosystem shaping children’s lives – including online platforms, messaging services, gaming environments, AI systems, immersive technologies and future digital services, among others – rather than regulating individual sectors in isolation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.9.2026) On 13 July 2026, the President of the Commission received the final report of the Co-Chairs of the Special Panel on Child Safety Online1. The report highlights the critical challenges faced by children online and sets out recommendations for better protecting and empowering them, as well as for an age-appropriate use of social media and other digital services. The report confirms that the EU has already established an ambitious and comprehensive framework for the protection of minors online, notably through the Digital Services Act2 and its Guidelines on the Protection of Minors Online3, the AI Act4, the General Data Protection Regulation5, the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive6, and the Better Internet for Kids strategy7. Complementing this framework, the Commission continues to support the colegislators in the ongoing negotiations on the proposed Regulation laying down rules to prevent and combat child sexual abuse8. The report of the Co-Chairs of the Special Panel advocates for a robust safety-by-design framework, as well as making sure that minors have access to age-appropriate digital spaces. The report also reflects a broad debate in Europe on issues such as age assurance, minimum age approaches for digital services, and the possibility of phased, age-appropriate access to specific functionalities. The Commission is now carefully assessing the report and its recommendations and will come forward with a proposal after the summer. In parallel, the Commission is preparing an action plan on the protection of children from crime, which will also follow up on relevant recommendations from the report.
1 Report from the Special panel on child safety online, https://commission.europa.eu/topics/digital-economy-and-

society/special-panel_en. 2 Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 on a Single Market For Digital Services, https://eurlex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj/eng. 3 Guidelines on measures to ensure a high level of privacy, safety and security for minors online, pursuant to Article 28(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=OJ:C_202505519. 4 Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence, https://eurlex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj/eng. 5 Regulation (EU) 2016/679 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data. 6 Directive 2005/29/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2005 concerning unfair business-to-consumer commercial practices in the internal market. 7 The new European strategy for a better internet for kids, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=COM:2022:212:FIN. 8 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council laying down rules to prevent and combat child sexual abuse, COM(2022) 209 final, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52022PC0209.
